title: Limiting Behavior of Non-Autonomous Stochastic Reversible Selkov Lattice Systems Driven by Locally Lipschitz Lévy Noises
summary: This work investigates the long-term distributional behavior of the reversible Selkov lattice systems defined on the set $\mathbb{Z}$ and driven by locally Lipschitz \emph{Lévy noises}, which possess two pairs of oppositely signed nonlinear terms and whose nonlinear couplings can grow polynomially with any order $p \geq 1$.
